objective: Reconstruct published CPVS membership using the official Table2 Seq/SourceID key, and rerun source-backed derivation after identifying the row-ordinal mapping defect.
previous_knowledge_consumed: PR #171: CPVS reconstruction gate fails closed on missing/failed audit evidence
PR #173: finite, non-zero magnitude check is applied to the final g/r intersection
Published Chen et al. (2020) ReadMe: Table2 Seq is the internal source identifier in bytes 24-29; ztf2g/ztf2r use Seq as the light-curve join key; Table2 has 781,602 rows while Seq spans 1..781,604
Published Chan et al. (2022) ReadMe: Table4 ZTF names identify the 730,184-object subset; earlier audit mapped names to parent row ordinal instead of the official Seq key

baseline.status: Historical membership figures derived by mapping published object names to Table2 row ordinals are invalid as a SourceID-space comparison. Exact CPVS reconstruction remains UNRESOLVED pending a fresh audit using the published Seq column.

expected_improvement: Parse official Table2 Seq identifiers for the source-id universe rather than manufacturing IDs from physical row ordinals.
Map published Table4 object names to their actual Table2 Seq values and reject duplicate names/IDs or unparseable identifiers.
Rerun source-backed derivation and independent published membership audit with the corrected ID semantics.
Keep the scientific gate fail-closed unless evidence-backed membership and selection criteria are resolved.

reproducibility.before: Prior audit mapped published ZTF names to one-based parent row ordinals, although source lightcurves use the published Table2 Seq field.
reproducibility.after: Code now reads the Table2 Seq/SourceID field; fresh heavy run is pending.

scientific_validity.before: The run reported 741,787 candidates, 725,101 intersection, 16,686 candidate-only and 5,083 published-only using a row-ordinal mapping; these membership differences are invalid and superseded.
scientific_validity.after: NOT_MEASURED: rerun using the official Seq identifiers is required before interpreting any candidate-only or published-only counts.

reliability.before: Source-provenance/readiness job was skipped on heavy refs.
reliability.after: The job executes successfully on heavy refs; source-backed scientific result still needs review.

evidence: Official CPVS ReadMe documents Table2 Seq at bytes 24-29 as the internal source identifier; ztf2g/ztf2r use the same Seq key. Source: https://cdsarc.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/ReadMe/J/ApJS/249/18?format=html&tex=true

Official CPVS Table2 contains 781,602 rows but its Seq ID range is 1..781,604, proving row ordinal is not a safe substitute for the identifier. Source: https://cdsarc.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/ReadMe/J/ApJS/249/18?format=html&tex=true

Official CPVS reconstruction Table4 supplies published ZTF names and an internal ID; audit now maps names to the parent's actual Seq values, not row ordinals. Source: https://cdsarc.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/ReadMe/J/ApJ/932/118?format=html&tex=true
Code changed in PR #176 commits ff65ca4, a5658a7, and ad93566; fresh CI/heavy source-backed validation has not yet been reviewed.

root_causes: Confirmed audit semantic defect: published names were converted to physical Table2 row numbers, while candidate and lightcurve membership use the catalog's Seq/SourceID identifier.
The derivation's parent source-ID universe also used row ordinals instead of the published Seq column.
Prior membership counts 725,101 intersection, 16,686 candidate-only and 5,083 published-only were produced in mismatched ID space and are invalid.

findings: Use the data dictionary's explicit key columns; row order is not a substitute for catalog identifiers.
Independent membership metrics are invalid unless candidate and published sets share the same documented identifier namespace.
A parser can map every name successfully and still produce a scientifically invalid comparison if the generated identifiers have the wrong semantics.
The source-backed rerun must publish both the Seq-keyed membership comparison and unambiguously identified unresolved selection criteria.

open_blockers: Run unit tests for non-contiguous Seq identifiers and fresh CI on the latest PR #176 head.
Run heavy source-backed derivation and confirm the parent catalog ID set is derived from Seq, with unique IDs.
Review the fresh name-to-Seq mapping, unmapped names, duplicate names/IDs, and candidate/published set differences.
Determine the remaining difference between source-backed SNR selection and the 730,184-object reference without tuning thresholds.
Keep Issue #170 open until the audit and selection semantics are evidence-backed.

knowledge_carried_forward: Never replace the official CPVS Seq identifier with row ordinal.
Do not hardcode IDs or tune thresholds to force cardinality equality.
Keep Issue #170 open until evidence supports closure.
Keep immutable v0.2.0 and released v1.0.1 unchanged.
